coreIdea: Complexity depends on pivot's split balance. ANY fixed-ratio split (not just 50-50) gives Θ(n log n). Worst case (extreme split every time) = Θ(n²).
mustRememberFormulas: Worst case (k=0 or n-1 every time): T(n)=T(n-1)+Θ(n) → Θ(n²)
Any fixed-ratio split: T(n)=T(αn)+T((1-α)n)+Θ(n) → Θ(n log n) for any constant 0<α≤1/2
Randomized QS: worst-case still Θ(n²) technically, but EXPECTED case Θ(n log n) for any input
P(pivot lands at worst position) = 2/n (pivot value = min or max)

commonTrapsQuickList: Quick Sort is NOT always O(n log n) — worst case is O(n²) with bad pivot choices
Any FIXED ratio split gives n log n, not just exact 50-50
Randomized QS worst-case is still Θ(n²) theoretically — only the EXPECTED case improves to n log n
Lomuto and Hoare partition schemes give different swap counts on the same input
highYieldPyqLessons: Split-ratio complexity derivation (7/15) is the dominant skill — internalize that 'any fixed fraction → n log n' generalization, it's tested with many different fractions.
Read worst-case vs expected-case wording VERY carefully for randomized quicksort questions — this exact distinction is the most repeated trap.
